proof_summary: Introduce the deficit between each suffix mass and its stable value; it evolves by \(D_{t+1}(j)=\lfloor(D_t(j-1)+D_t(j))/2\rfloor\), and stability occurs exactly when the final relevant deficit vanishes. A coupling of the deficits for masses \(n\) and \(n+1\), together with leftward propagation of zero deficits, shows that the latter cannot drain before time \(a(n)+1\) and must drain by time \(a(n)+2\).
